source.name: Transaction Tokens For Agents
source.status: active individual Internet-Draft; informational; not an IETF WG standard

scenario: A low-assurance external agent initiates a transaction that later passes through a strongly verified internal agent, policy service, execution service, and database.

facts.meaning: The transaction can retain the delegated agent identity separately from the represented principal.
The transaction context identifies the agent currently executing the request and updates it when the next agent obtains a replacement token.
facts.reason: AuditSpec has an immediate actor concept, but no executable agentic_ctx parser/profile yet.

facts.meaning: The first agent in the transaction chain remains immutable as the originator.
facts.reason: AuditSpec can preserve the participant and provenance, but originator has no dedicated first-class Core field.

facts.meaning: The number of agent transitions is incremented during agent replacement flows.
facts.reason: AuditSpec can derive graph/path length in some contexts, but it does not currently accept this token-supplied hop counter as a defined semantic assertion.

facts.meaning: Overall agent-chain assurance is monotonically attenuated to the minimum assurance level encountered in the chain.
Authorization-relevant agent context must come from a verified source rather than self-report when it influences policy.
facts.reason: AuditSpec models producer trust and authority boundaries, but does not define an Agent Registry protocol.

facts.meaning: The requesting workload chain remains available alongside agent-specific context.
facts.reason: AuditSpec can retain workload participants but lacks a dedicated req_wl projection.

facts.meaning: Deployments may attach verified agent posture, provenance, and workload metadata.
facts.reason: AuditSpec intentionally avoids standardizing deployment-specific agent posture fields without a separate profile.

facts.meaning: A high-assurance internal agent must not make a low-assurance external originator appear high assurance downstream.
